_comment: Model configuration for Episodic. This file defines available models, their types, and parameters.
_pricing_note: Optional pricing can be added to any model. Format: {"input": 3.0, "output": 15.0, "unit": "per_1m_tokens", "last_updated": "YYYY-MM-DD"}

models.name: gpt-4o-mini
models.description: OpenAI's most cost-effective model, designed for fast responses at scale. GPT-4o Mini offers strong performance on everyday tasks while being significantly cheaper than larger models. It handles general conversation, simple coding questions, and basic analysis well, though it may struggle with complex reasoning or specialized domains.
weaknesses: May miss nuance in difficult tasks

models.name: gpt-4o
models.description: OpenAI's flagship multimodal model optimized for speed and efficiency. GPT-4o matches GPT-4 Turbo's intelligence while being 2x faster and 50% cheaper. It excels at complex reasoning, coding, and creative tasks. The 'o' stands for 'omni' - it can process text, images, and audio natively.
weaknesses: May be overkill for simple tasks

models.name: o3
models.description: OpenAI's advanced reasoning model, designed for complex problem-solving tasks requiring step-by-step thinking. o3 uses chain-of-thought reasoning internally before producing its response, making it exceptionally strong at math, coding challenges, and logical puzzles. Best for tasks where accuracy matters more than speed.

models.name: o4-mini
models.description: OpenAI's efficient reasoning model, offering o-series reasoning capabilities at a lower cost. o4-mini brings chain-of-thought reasoning to more budget-conscious applications while maintaining strong performance on math, coding, and logical tasks. A good middle ground between speed and reasoning depth.
weaknesses: Less capable than o3 on hard problems
May be overkill for simple tasks

models.name: gpt-3.5-turbo
models.description: OpenAI's legacy fast and affordable model. GPT-3.5 Turbo was the model that powered the original ChatGPT and remains useful for simple tasks where cost is critical. While largely superseded by GPT-4o Mini, it's still available for existing applications and budget-conscious use cases.

models.name: gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct
models.description: An instruction-tuned variant of GPT-3.5 optimized for completing single-turn tasks. Unlike the chat model, this version is designed for direct instruction following without conversational context. Useful for structured tasks like text transformation, extraction, and formatting.

models.name: gpt-4
models.description: OpenAI's original GPT-4 model that marked a major leap in AI capabilities. While now superseded by GPT-4o and GPT-4 Turbo, the original GPT-4 remains available for users who need its specific behavior. Known for strong reasoning and reduced hallucinations compared to GPT-3.5.

models.name: gpt-5
models.description: OpenAI's next-generation flagship model, representing a significant capability jump from GPT-4. GPT-5 features improved reasoning, coding, and creative abilities with a massive 272K context window. It's designed to handle more complex tasks with greater accuracy and nuance than its predecessors.
weaknesses: May be overkill for simple tasks

models.name: gpt-5.1
models.description: An incremental update to GPT-5, offering refinements and improvements based on user feedback. GPT-5.1 maintains the same pricing and context window as GPT-5 while providing better instruction following and reduced edge-case failures. OpenAI's current recommended model for most use cases.
weaknesses: May be overkill for simple tasks

models.name: claude-opus-4-1-20250805
models.description: The most capable model in the Claude family, designed for highly complex tasks requiring deep reasoning and analysis. Opus 4.1 excels at research, complex coding projects, and tasks requiring extensive knowledge synthesis. It's significantly more expensive than Sonnet but offers superior performance on difficult problems.

models.name: claude-sonnet-4-20250522
models.description: Anthropic's flagship balanced model, offering strong reasoning and coding abilities at moderate cost. Claude Sonnet 4 excels at nuanced conversation, code generation, and analytical tasks. It's particularly good at following complex instructions and maintaining context over long conversations. A solid all-around choice that balances capability with affordability.
strengths: Works well for chat and instruct tasks

models.name: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929
models.description: An updated version of Claude Sonnet 4 with refinements and improvements. Sonnet 4.5 maintains the same balanced capabilities as its predecessor while offering better performance on edge cases and improved instruction following. A strong all-around choice for most tasks.
strengths: Good balance of cost and capability

models.name: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
models.description: Anthropic's fastest and most affordable Claude model. Haiku 4.5 is optimized for speed while maintaining strong capabilities. It's ideal for tasks that need quick responses at scale, like summarization, simple analysis, and high-volume applications. While not as capable as Sonnet for complex reasoning, it handles most everyday tasks well.
weaknesses: Not ideal for difficult coding tasks

models.name: gemini-2.5-pro
models.description: Google's most capable Gemini model with an industry-leading 2M token context window. Gemini 2.5 Pro excels at analyzing large documents, codebases, and long conversations. It offers strong reasoning and multimodal capabilities (text, images, video, audio). Particularly powerful for tasks requiring understanding of extensive context.
weaknesses: Can be slower on very long contexts

models.name: gemini-2.5-flash
models.description: Google's fast and efficient Gemini model, optimized for speed while maintaining strong capabilities. Flash offers a 1M token context window at lower cost than Pro, making it ideal for applications requiring quick responses and large document processing. Good balance of speed and capability.
weaknesses: Less capable than Pro on complex tasks

models.name: gemini-2.5-flash-lite
models.description: The most lightweight Gemini model, designed for maximum speed and cost efficiency. Flash-Lite is ideal for simple tasks, high-volume applications, and latency-sensitive use cases. While less capable than Flash or Pro, it still benefits from the 1M context window.

models.name: llama3.3
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's latest open-weight large language model, offering strong general capabilities comparable to many commercial models. Llama 3.3 runs locally via Ollama, meaning no API costs and full data privacy. The 70B parameter size provides excellent performance but requires significant VRAM (40GB+ recommended for full precision).
weaknesses: Slower than cloud models on modest hardware

models.name: llama3
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's Llama 3 8B model running locally via Ollama. A capable general-purpose model that runs efficiently on consumer hardware. Good for everyday tasks and conversation while keeping data fully private on your machine.

models.name: llama3:instruct
models.creator: Meta
models.description: The instruction-tuned variant of Llama 3 8B, optimized for following instructions and completing tasks. Better than the chat variant for structured tasks like summarization, extraction, and analysis. Runs locally with full privacy.

models.name: mistral
models.creator: Mistral AI
models.description: Mistral AI's efficient 7B model, known for punching above its weight class. Despite its small size, Mistral 7B outperforms larger models on many benchmarks. Runs quickly on consumer hardware with low memory requirements, making it an excellent choice for local inference.
weaknesses: May need more guidance than larger models

models.name: mistral:instruct
models.creator: Mistral AI
models.description: The instruction-tuned version of Mistral 7B, optimized for following commands and completing structured tasks. Better than the chat variant for specific tasks like extraction, summarization, and analysis. Very efficient on consumer hardware.

models.name: codellama
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's code-specialized model based on Llama 2, designed for code completion and generation. As a base model, it's optimized for completing code rather than following instructions. Best for IDE-style code completion tasks.

models.name: phi3
models.creator: Microsoft
models.description: Microsoft's small but mighty language model. Phi-3 achieves impressive capabilities despite its tiny 3.8B size, thanks to high-quality training data. Runs on almost any hardware including laptops without dedicated GPUs. Great for experimentation and resource-constrained environments.

models.name: phi4
models.creator: Microsoft
models.description: Microsoft's larger Phi model, scaling up the efficient architecture to 14B parameters. Phi-4 offers significantly better capabilities than Phi-3 while still running on consumer GPUs. Strong performance on reasoning and coding tasks relative to its size.

models.name: llama4-scout
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's Llama 4 Scout, one of the smaller models in the Llama 4 family. Scout is designed for efficient deployment while maintaining strong general capabilities. Part of Meta's next-generation open model series.

models.name: llama4-maverick
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's flagship Llama 4 model, offering the highest capabilities in the Llama 4 series. Maverick represents Meta's most powerful open-weight model, competitive with commercial offerings. Requires significant hardware but delivers exceptional performance.

models.name: deepseek-r1
models.creator: DeepSeek
models.description: DeepSeek's R1 is a powerful open-source reasoning model that rivals GPT-4 and Claude at a fraction of the cost. It excels at step-by-step reasoning, math, and coding tasks. R1 runs locally via Ollama, offering full privacy and no per-token costs. The model uses chain-of-thought reasoning visible in its output.
weaknesses: Can be verbose with reasoning steps
Newer model with less community support

models.name: openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.1
models.description: Claude Opus 4.1 accessed via OpenRouter. OpenRouter provides a unified API to multiple providers, often with competitive pricing and additional features like automatic failover. Same capabilities as direct API access.
strengths: Single API key for multiple providers

models.name: openrouter/openai/gpt-4
models.description: OpenAI's GPT-4 accessed via OpenRouter. Same capabilities as direct API access but through OpenRouter's unified interface.

models.name: openrouter/openai/gpt-3.5-turbo
models.description: OpenAI's GPT-3.5 Turbo via OpenRouter. Budget-friendly option for simple tasks through OpenRouter's unified API.

models.name: openrouter/google/gemini-2.5-pro
models.description: Google's Gemini 2.5 Pro via OpenRouter. Access Google's powerful model through OpenRouter's unified API with potential pricing advantages.

models.name: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-r1
models.description: DeepSeek's R1 reasoning model via OpenRouter. Excellent for complex reasoning and math tasks, accessed through OpenRouter's unified API without running locally.

models.name: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3
models.description: DeepSeek's Chat V3 model via OpenRouter. A strong general-purpose chat model from DeepSeek, known for competitive performance at lower cost.

models.name: openrouter/meta-llama/llama-4-scout:free
models.description: Meta's Llama 4 Scout accessed via OpenRouter's free tier. A cost-effective way to try Llama 4 models without local hardware or API costs.

models.name: openrouter/meta-llama/llama-4-maverick:free
models.description: Meta's flagship Llama 4 Maverick via OpenRouter's free tier. Access the most powerful Llama 4 model without local hardware or API costs.

models.name: openrouter/mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct
models.description: Mistral AI's efficient 7B instruct model via OpenRouter. Great value for instruction-following tasks without local hardware requirements.

models.name: openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct
models.description: Meta's powerful Llama 3.3 70B instruction model via OpenRouter. Strong capabilities rivaling commercial models, accessible without local hardware through OpenRouter's API.

models.name: openrouter/qwen/qwen-2-72b-instruct
models.creator: Alibaba
models.description: Alibaba's Qwen 2 72B instruction model via OpenRouter. A powerful Chinese-developed model with strong multilingual capabilities, particularly in Chinese and English.

models.name: openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k2
models.creator: Moonshot AI
models.description: Moonshot AI's Kimi K2 via OpenRouter. A powerful Chinese AI model with strong long-context capabilities and 128K token window. Known for competitive performance on benchmarks.

models.name: openrouter/databricks/dbrx-instruct
models.creator: Databricks
models.description: Databricks' DBRX 132B instruction model via OpenRouter. A large open-source model designed for enterprise use cases with strong performance on coding and analysis tasks.

models.name: openrouter/nousresearch/hermes-3-405b-instruct
models.creator: Nous Research
models.description: Nous Research's massive Hermes 3 405B instruction model via OpenRouter. Built on the largest Llama base, Hermes models are known for creative and unconstrained outputs, popular in the open-source community.

models.name: openrouter/mistralai/mixtral-8x7b-instruct
models.creator: Mistral AI
models.description: Mistral AI's Mixture of Experts model via OpenRouter. Mixtral uses 8 expert networks (7B each) with sparse activation, providing strong performance while only using ~12B parameters per forward pass. Excellent efficiency-to-quality ratio.
weaknesses: Less capable than larger dense models

models.name: huggingface/meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's Llama 3 8B model accessible via HuggingFace inference. A capable smaller model good for general tasks, running on HuggingFace's infrastructure without requiring local hardware.

models.name: huggingface/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's latest open-weight model fine-tuned for instruction following. Llama 3.3 70B Instruct excels at following complex instructions, coding, analysis, and multi-step reasoning. At 70B parameters, it rivals many commercial models while being freely accessible via HuggingFace. Ideal for users who want strong capabilities without API costs.

models.name: huggingface/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's latest open-weight large language model in its base (pre-trained) form. This is the raw foundational model without instruction tuning, making it suitable for fine-tuning or specialized applications. At 70 billion parameters, it offers strong general capabilities rivaling many commercial models. Accessed via HuggingFace's inference API, so no local hardware required.
strengths: No API costs via HuggingFace free tier
weaknesses: Not instruction-tuned (use Instruct version for chat)

models.name: huggingface/meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-70B
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's Llama 3 70B via HuggingFace. A powerful large model with strong general capabilities, though superseded by Llama 3.3. Accessible without local hardware through HuggingFace's inference API.

models.name: huggingface/meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's Llama 4 Scout via HuggingFace inference. Access the efficient Llama 4 model through HuggingFace without local hardware requirements.

models.name: huggingface/meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's flagship Llama 4 Maverick model via HuggingFace inference. The larger, more capable version of Llama 4, designed for complex reasoning and generation tasks. Accessible through HuggingFace without local hardware requirements.

models.name: huggingface/meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat
models.creator: Meta
models.description: Meta's Llama 2 7B Chat model via HuggingFace. An older but proven model fine-tuned for conversational tasks. Still useful for lighter workloads and legacy compatibility, though superseded by Llama 3.x series.

models.name: huggingface/Qwen/Qwen-3
models.creator: Alibaba
models.description: Alibaba's Qwen 3 model via HuggingFace inference. Part of the competitive Qwen series known for strong multilingual capabilities, particularly Chinese and English. Offers excellent performance on reasoning and coding tasks.

models.name: huggingface/mistralai/Mistral-Small-3.1
models.creator: Mistral AI
models.description: Mistral AI's Small 3.1 model via HuggingFace. A compact yet capable model from the European AI lab known for efficient architectures. Optimized for fast inference while maintaining quality, ideal for latency-sensitive applications.

models.name: huggingface/mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1
models.creator: Mistral AI
models.description: Mistral AI's groundbreaking Mixture of Experts model via HuggingFace. Uses 8 expert networks (7B each) with sparse activation, achieving strong performance while only activating ~12B parameters per forward pass. This architecture provides an excellent efficiency-to-quality ratio.

models.name: huggingface/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528
models.creator: DeepSeek
models.description: DeepSeek's R1-0528 reasoning model via HuggingFace. Part of the R1 series known for exceptional reasoning capabilities through chain-of-thought processing. DeepSeek models have gained recognition for strong performance at competitive costs, particularly in math and coding benchmarks.

models.name: huggingface/google/gemma-7b
models.creator: Google
models.description: Google's Gemma 7B model via HuggingFace. An open-weight model from Google designed to be lightweight yet capable. Part of the Gemma family built using similar technology to Gemini. Good for general tasks where you want Google's quality in an open model.

models.name: huggingface/01-ai/Yi-1.5-34B-Chat
models.creator: 01.AI
models.description: 01.AI's Yi 1.5 34B Chat model via HuggingFace. A strong bilingual (Chinese/English) model from the startup founded by Kai-Fu Lee. At 34B parameters, it offers a good balance of capability and efficiency, known for strong performance on Chinese language tasks and competitive English abilities.

models.name: huggingface/bigscience/bloom
models.creator: BigScience
models.description: BigScience's BLOOM 176B via HuggingFace. A massive open-science multilingual model trained by a collaborative of researchers. Supports 46 natural languages and 13 programming languages. As a base model, it's designed for text generation and fine-tuning rather than chat.

models.name: huggingface/EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b
models.creator: EleutherAI
models.description: EleutherAI's GPT-NeoX 20B via HuggingFace. A pioneering open-source large language model from the nonprofit EleutherAI research collective. As a base model, it excels at text generation and completion tasks. Important for the open-source AI movement, though superseded by newer models.
